Fit a set of detection functions and compare them

Source: R/sweep.R
sweep_models.Rd

Fits every candidate in a model_set() to the same data at the same truncation, using mrds::ddf(), and returns a selection table. Use it to choose a detection function for a survey.

Usage

sweep_models(
  data,
  models = NULL,
  truncation,
  left = NULL,
  breaks = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with one row per detection. Needs a distance column for exact distances, or distbegin and distend for binned ones. The flatfile from distsamp::detection_data() has this shape. Rows with no distance (samples without a detection) are dropped.

models

A model_set(). NULL (default) uses model_set().

truncation

Number. Right truncation distance, in the units of the distances. Required, with no default.

left

Number. Left truncation distance, for a platform that cannot see beneath itself. NULL (default) for none.

breaks

Numeric vector of bin cutpoints, for binned data. NULL (default) derives them from distbegin and distend. Ignored, with a warning, for exact distances.

quiet

Logical. TRUE suppresses the summary message. Default FALSE.

Value

An object of class dsfit_sweep, a list with:

table

The selection table, one row per candidate including failures. See selection_table() for the columns.

fits

List of ddf objects named by model_id. NULL for a candidate that failed.

settings

List with truncation, left, binned, breaks, n (detections fitted), n_dropped (rows removed during preparation) and failures (first line of the error, or "did not converge", named by model_id).

How it works

  1. Checks that mrds is installed, that models is a model set, and that truncation is a single positive number.

  2. Prepares the data with prepare_distance_data(): validates the distances, drops rows with no distance or outside the truncation, and decides whether the fit is binned.

  3. Warns if left is set and the model set contains the gamma key.

  4. Fits each candidate with mrds::ddf(). A candidate that errors or does not converge is recorded as a failure and the sweep continues.

  5. Builds the selection table, sorted by AIC, and prints a short report unless quiet = TRUE.

Truncation is one value per sweep

AIC only compares models fitted to the same data. A different truncation keeps a different set of detections, so the AICs are not comparable. To compare truncations, run one sweep per truncation and check whether the chosen model and its p stay stable.

What the table reports besides AIC

The effective strip half-width (esw) is the width of a strip in which detection is certain that would yield the same expected number of detections. It goes directly into density. Two models within 2 AIC of each other can have quite different esw, so the table reports p (average detection probability), its standard error and CV, and esw next to AIC.

A goodness-of-fit p-value is also reported. The null hypothesis is that the fitted function describes the observed distances, so a small p-value is evidence against the model. The top AIC model can still fail this test.

Which goodness-of-fit test to read

Exact distances get a Cramer-von Mises test (cvm_p), which tests their empirical distribution. Binned distances have no empirical distribution, so they get a chi-square test over the survey's own bins (chisq_p). chisq_p is also filled in for exact distances, but over cutpoints mrds chooses; read cvm_p there. Printing a sweep shows the test that applies.

A chi-square test over few bins can have no degrees of freedom left (for example three bins and a two-parameter key). mrds then returns NA. The model converged; it just has no chi-square test.

Binned and exact distances cannot be mixed

Distances from STRIP records are intervals and are fitted binned. Distances from angles or positions are exact. The two likelihoods differ, so their AICs are not comparable. Data containing both is refused; split it and run one sweep for each.

Left truncation and the gamma key

Both model a platform that cannot see directly beneath itself. Using both accounts for the blind spot twice, so setting left for a model set that contains the gamma key gives a warning.

Monotonicity constraint

As in Distance::ds(), a candidate with adjustment terms and no covariates is fitted with a strict monotonicity constraint (mono = TRUE, mono.strict = TRUE in mrds). This stops g(x), the detection probability at distance x, from exceeding 1 or turning upward. AIC and p then match ds() with its defaults. Covariate models are unconstrained, as in ds(). The gamma key is also unconstrained, because it rises to a peak by design.

g(0) is assumed to be 1

Every fit assumes an animal on the track-line is always detected. A wrong g(0) scales every candidate by the same factor, so model selection cannot detect it. Correct for it at the abundance step, from external sources, and propagate its standard error (see g0()).

References

Miller, D.L., Rexstad, E., Thomas, L., Marshall, L. and Laake, J.L. (2019) Distance sampling in R. Journal of Statistical Software 89(1):1-28. doi:10.18637/jss.v089.i01

Buckland, S.T., Anderson, D.R., Burnham, K.P., Laake, J.L., Borchers, D.L. and Thomas, L. (2001) Introduction to Distance Sampling. Oxford University Press.

See also

model_set(), selection_table()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(object = 1:200, distance = abs(rnorm(200, 0, 120)))
d <- d[d$distance < 400, ]

sw <- sweep_models(d, model_set(c("hn", "hr", "gamma")), truncation = 400)
#> Fitted 3 of 3 candidate models to 200 detections, truncation 400.
#>   g(0) = 1 is assumed; see `?sweep_models`.
sw
#> <dsfit_sweep>
#>   detections:  200
#>   truncation:  400
#>   models:      3 of 3 fitted
#> 
#>  model  dAIC      p  p_cv   esw CvM_p
#>     hn  0.00 0.3494 0.052 139.8 0.928
#>  gamma  9.92 0.3010 0.074 120.4 0.498
#>     hr 10.18 0.3781 0.064 151.3 0.786
#> 
#>   Rank on esw and p_cv as well as dAIC: models within 2 AIC can
#>   imply materially different abundance. g(0) = 1 is assumed.

# Compare esw and p_cv as well as delta AIC
selection_table(sw)[, c("model_id", "delta_aic", "p", "p_cv", "esw")]
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   model_id delta_aic     p   p_cv   esw
#>   <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 hn            0    0.349 0.0525  140.
#> 2 gamma         9.92 0.301 0.0737  120.
#> 3 hr           10.2  0.378 0.0638  151.
